roots.gloss: a natural watercourse flowing to the sea or a lake
to flow, to move continuously
stream, brook, small watercourse
mystery, secret, whispered counsel
stream, brook, channel of water

annotations.notes: Opening word of the Wake, completing the broken sentence from p.628. Vico's ricorso: the river's return enacts the cyclical theory of history. The compound collapses river (en) and runa (non: mystery) — the Wake's own mystery is waterborne.

roots.gloss: gone by in time; beyond in space
step, pace; having suffered, undergone
past, gone, elapsed

annotations.notes: La 'passus' carries both the spatial sense (pace, stride) and the participial sense of suffering (cf. Passion). The Viconian first age begins with a fall past the threshold of divine thunder.

roots.gloss: the first woman; biblical mother of humanity
life, living; the Hebrew name of Eve
Irish form of Eve; also a variant of the name Aoife

annotations.notes: Eve and Adam inverted from Genesis order. He 'Chavah' (life) links Eve to Anna Livia Plurabelle as the life-giving river. The Church of Adam and Eve (Merchant's Quay, Dublin) stands on the south bank of the Liffey.

roots.gloss: the first man; biblical progenitor
earth, ground, red clay; the substance from which Adam was formed
red; cognate with adamah and edom
surface of the earth, skin

annotations.notes: He 'adamah' (earth/red clay) grounds HCE in the material world; Malkuth is the lowest sefirah, the Kingdom, the earthly realm. The inversion Eve-Adam-Adam-Eve enacts the cyclical chiasmus fundamental to the Wake's structure.

roots.gloss: to deviate suddenly from a straight course
to file, to abrade, to wear away by friction
to whirr, to buzz, to move rapidly with a vibrating motion
the Epicurean swerve of atoms; Lucretian deviation from determinism

annotations.notes: The Lucretian clinamen (atomic swerve) underlies the English sense. Non 'sverfa' (to file/abrade) suggests the river wearing at the shoreline. The swerve is both geographic (the river's bend) and philosophical (the deviation that makes free will possible).

roots.gloss: to handle or use with skill, especially a weapon
to engage in battle or combat
again, once more; prefix expressing repetition
world war; global conflict
fury, rage, fierce anger in battle

annotations.notes: De 'wieder' (again) activates the Viconian return: battles recur. 'Wielderfight' echoes Waterloo (Wellington/Napoleon), the central HCE sin-myth. Gevurah (Strength/Judgement) is the sefirah of power and severity in combat.

roots.gloss: convenient, suitable, advantageous, comfortable
Roman emperor AD 177–192; known for vanity and gladiatorial excess
roomy, spacious, affording ample room
a chest of drawers; a toilet (later French derivative)

annotations.notes: La 'commodus' puns on Vico Road (Dalkey, Dublin) and on the Viconian cyclical system. Emperor Commodus represents aristocratic overreach and imperial decadence (Vico cycle 2 → 3 transition). The scatological overtone (commode) is consistent with Joyce's earthward humour.

roots.gloss: headland peninsula north of Dublin Bay; Howth Head
Éadar's peak; the Irish name for Howth Head
head; the Norse name giving rise to the anglicised Howth
head (of the body); headland, promontory

annotations.notes: Howth Castle and Environs (HCE) = initials of the protagonist Here Comes Everybody / Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker. The sleeping giant (Finn MacCool) lies with his head at Howth, his feet at the Phoenix Park. Non 'hǫfuð' (head) links to Kether (Crown), the highest sefirah, the divine head.
